equation_request.abstract:
We give a quantum algorithm for evaluating formulas over an extended gate set, including all twoand three-bit binary gates (e.g., NAND, 3-majority). The algorithm is optimal on read-once formulas for which each gate's inputs are balanced in a certain sense.

The main new tool is a correspondence between a classical linear-algebraic model of computation, "span programs," and weighted bipartite graphs. A span program's evaluation corresponds to an eigenvalue-zero eigenvector of the associated graph. A quantum computer can therefore evaluate the span program by applying spectral estimation to the graph.

For example, the classical complexity of evaluating the balanced ternary majority formula is unknown, and the natural generalization of randomized alpha-beta pruning is known to be suboptimal. In contrast, our algorithm generalizes the optimal quantum AND-OR formula evaluation algorithm and is optimal for evaluating the balanced ternary majority formula.

specification.problem: Decide f(x) for a read-once formula over an extended gate set by building a weighted bipartite graph G_P(x) from a span program P for f, then running phase estimation of the walk U=R_B R_A started at the output vertex |r>, and accepting if the phase register reads 0.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Smallest useful instance (assumed): a single 2-input NAND/AND span program with fixed small explicit edge weights on a few vertices. Build the oracle-dependent walk, run a small phase estimation, and read the all-zero acceptance probability. Out of scope: composition for nested formulas, the balance-condition analysis, optimality proofs, the paper's exact span-program-to-graph weight formulas, the 3-majority and general 2- and 3-bit gate span programs, and the N^0.753 and 2.5^d scaling claims.

symbols.meaning: input bits accessed through the oracle
weighted bipartite graph built from span program P and input x
normalized weighted adjacency matrix of G_P(x)

equations.label: Oracle
equations.description: Coherent query access to the input bits, one query per placement.
equations.justification: Standard query oracle, taken from the sketch rather than the abstract.
assumptions: Oracle gives coherent access to x

equations.label: Zero-eigenvector criterion
equations.description: A true formula gives a zero-eigenvalue eigenvector of the graph. A false formula gives a spectral gap of order 1/sqrt(W).
equations.abstract_quote: A span program's evaluation corresponds to an eigenvalue-zero eigenvector of the associated graph.
equations.justification: The abstract states the zero-eigenvector correspondence. The gap scale and false-case behaviour come from the sketch.
assumptions: Gap scale 1/sqrt(W) is from the sketch, not the abstract

equations.label: Walk as two reflections
equations.description: Each reflection is about the span of the stars of the left or right vertices. The x-dependent reflection uses oracle calls to keep or remove input edges.
equations.abstract_quote: A quantum computer can therefore evaluate the span program by applying spectral estimation to the graph.
equations.justification: Spectral estimation of a graph suggests a walk built from two reflections, as in the AND-OR algorithm. The details are recalled, not stated.
assumptions: Star states are normalized using span-program weights

equations.label: Eigenphase relation
equations.description: Eigenphases of U are the arccos of the eigenvalues of the normalized adjacency matrix. So lambda=0 maps to theta=pi/2 on the plain walk, and the sketch's 'phase 0' needs a convention such as a shifted walk. The sketch states that the zero eigenspace corresponds to phase 0.
equations.justification: Standard spectral relation for a product of two reflections. The mapping of lambda=0 to phase 0 is unresolved.
assumptions: Convention for lambda=0 versus phase 0 fixed by a shift

equations.label: Phase estimation acceptance
equations.description: Accept on the all-zero phase outcome, which is the theta_0 outcome under the convention in eq_4. The overlap is large if f=1 and small if f=0.
equations.justification: Sketch-level design with precision tied to the gap. The constants are not given.
assumptions: Precision set by the known gap

registers.name: query
registers.role: index and answer bit for O_x; uncomputed after each use

specification.initial_state: vertex register in |r>, phase register Hadamards on |0^m>, ancillas |0>

steps.description: Choose a tiny gate (NAND or AND) and write its span program with explicit vectors and witness size W. This is an assumed instance, and the oracle O_x supplies the input bits for it.
Build G_P(x) with weights from the span program vectors. Input edges are kept or removed according to x_i via O_x. A true formula gives a zero-eigenvector and a false one gives a gap.
Implement U=R_B R_A, with the x-dependent reflection using oracle calls, then uncompute the query register. Fix the phase convention so that the zero eigenspace maps to the accepted phase.
Run phase estimation with controlled powers of U from |r>, using about sqrt(W) applications of U.
Measure the phase register and accept on all zeros. Repeat a constant number of times and take a majority vote.

specification.measurement: Measure only the phase register. Qiskit is little-endian, so bit i of the counts string is bits[::-1][i]. Accept on the all-zero outcome.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Majority vote over a constant number of repetitions of the accept/reject outcome.
assumptions: Smallest instance chosen: a single gate span program with explicit weights
Constant-factor error reduction by repetition is allowed
Phase 0 versus eigenvalue 0 is handled by a convention
missing_information: Exact composition and balance rule for nested gates
Precise reflections and the mapping of lambda=0 to phase 0
Constants for phase estimation precision and acceptance thresholds
The paper's explicit span programs for 3-majority and general 2- and 3-bit gates
